note: Synthetic data for the search benchmark (Spike 2). Every person, place and number is invented.

memories.title: Keep answers short
memories.body: I prefer concise answers: lead with the answer, then at most three short paragraphs of supporting detail. Skip preambles like "Great question".

memories.title: Bullet points for options
memories.body: When comparing options, use a bulleted list or a small table rather than long prose.

memories.title: No emojis
memories.body: Don't use emojis in anything you write for me, including commit messages, documents and chat replies.

memories.title: British spelling in writing
memories.body: Use British English spelling (colour, organise, licence) in documents and emails. Code identifiers can stay American.

memories.title: Email tone with clients
memories.body: Client emails should be warm but brief: greet them by first name, two or three short paragraphs, a clear next step, and sign off with "Best, Sam".

memories.title: Writing to my family in Spanish
memories.body: I write to my parents and my sister in Spanish (Rioplatense, using "vos"). Messages to them should be informal and affectionate.

memories.title: How I like feedback
memories.body: Give direct critical feedback first, then what works. I'd rather hear that a plan has a flaw than be reassured.

memories.title: Meeting notes format
memories.body: Meeting summaries: decisions first, then action items with an owner and a date, then open questions. No transcript-style narration.

memories.title: Technical depth of explanations
memories.body: I'm a senior engineer: skip beginner explanations of programming concepts, but do explain unfamiliar domain terms (medical, legal, tax).

memories.title: Ask before assuming
memories.body: If a request is ambiguous in a way that changes the result, ask one clarifying question instead of guessing. For small details, pick a sensible default and say so.

memories.title: Slack style with the Harbor team
memories.body: Slack messages to the Harbor team should be one or two lines, no headings; use threads for anything longer.

memories.title: Dates and times
memories.body: Use 24-hour time and day-month-year dates (16 Oct 2026). My time zone is Europe/Lisbon.

memories.title: Metric units
memories.body: Use metric units: kilometres, kilograms, degrees Celsius. Convert recipes from cups and ounces to grams and millilitres.

memories.title: No flattery
memories.body: Don't praise my questions or ideas. A neutral, matter-of-fact tone works best for me.

memories.title: Blog writing voice
memories.body: For my blog posts: first person, plain words, short sentences, one idea per paragraph, and no marketing language like "unlock" or "supercharge".

memories.title: Slide decks
memories.body: Slides should carry one message each and at most 20 words of text; put the detail in the speaker notes.

memories.title: Summaries of articles
memories.body: When summarizing an article, give a three-sentence summary and then the one claim I should double-check.

memories.title: When you make a mistake
memories.body: If you got something wrong, say what was wrong and fix it. No long apologies.

memories.title: Learning Portuguese
memories.body: I'm learning European Portuguese (around A2). When I ask, correct my Portuguese gently and explain the grammar rule in English.

memories.title: Prefer async communication
memories.body: I prefer async written communication over calls. Suggest a call only when a thread has gone back and forth more than three times.

memories.title: Proposals to new clients
memories.body: Proposals should start with the client's problem in their own words, then scope, timeline, price, and what is out of scope.

memories.title: Long documents
memories.body: Documents longer than a page need headings and a short summary at the top.

memories.title: Language with the sailing club
memories.body: Emails to the sailing club can be in English; they usually reply in Portuguese, which I can read slowly.

memories.title: Coffee order
memories.body: Oat milk flat white, no sugar. If oat milk isn't available, a black americano.

memories.title: Coffee at home
memories.body: On weekend mornings I make pour-over coffee with a V60 and light-roast beans, ground fresh.

memories.title: Favourite café to work from
memories.body: I work from Café Lume most Tuesday and Thursday mornings: good wifi, quiet until 11.

memories.title: Vegetarian
memories.body: I've been vegetarian since 2019. I eat eggs and dairy but no meat or fish, including fish sauce and gelatin.

memories.title: Favourite cuisines
memories.body: I love Japanese, Ethiopian and South Indian food. Not a fan of very sweet desserts.

memories.title: Focus music
memories.body: For deep work I listen to ambient or instrumental post-rock; lyrics distract me.

memories.title: Reading taste
memories.body: I read mostly science fiction and popular history, and prefer paper books to e-books.

memories.title: Travel style
memories.body: I prefer trains over flights for trips under six hours, aisle seats, and small guesthouses over big hotel chains.

memories.title: Sailing
memories.body: I sail dinghies at the Tejo Sailing Club on weekends from April to October.

memories.title: Bouldering
memories.body: I go bouldering twice a week, usually Monday and Wednesday evenings.

memories.title: Running routine
memories.body: I run three times a week, about 30 km in total, mostly along the river early in the morning.

memories.title: Best hours for focused work
memories.body: I do my best focused work between 7:00 and 11:00. Avoid scheduling meetings for me before 11:00.

memories.title: Desk setup
memories.body: I use a standing desk, a split keyboard and a single 27-inch monitor.

memories.title: Houseplants
memories.body: I keep about fifteen houseplants, mostly tropical, and I'm bad at remembering to water them.

memories.title: Balcony garden
memories.body: I grow tomatoes, basil and chillies on the balcony; I usually plant in March.

memories.title: My cat
memories.body: I have a grey cat called Miso, six years old and indoor only. A neighbour feeds her when I travel.

memories.title: Gift ideas for Jordan
memories.body: Jordan likes ceramics, specialty tea and hiking gear. Avoid scented candles.

memories.title: Partner
memories.body: My partner is Jordan; we've lived together since 2022. Jordan is a nurse who works rotating shifts.

memories.title: Sister
memories.body: My sister Lucía lives in Montevideo with her two kids, aged 8 and 5.

memories.title: Parents
memories.body: My parents live in Buenos Aires. I call them on Sunday afternoons, Lisbon time.

memories.title: Family birthdays
memories.body: Jordan's birthday is 12 March and Lucía's is 30 July. Remind me two weeks ahead so I can send something.

memories.title: Clothing sizes
memories.body: Shirt size M, trousers 32/32, shoes EU 43.

memories.title: Films
memories.body: I like slow science fiction and documentaries. I dislike horror.

memories.title: Podcasts
memories.body: On runs I listen to podcasts about history and economics; no true crime.

memories.title: Cooking on weeknights
memories.body: I cook most weeknights and like one-pot recipes that take under 40 minutes. I have a pressure cooker and a cast-iron pan.

memories.title: Languages I speak
memories.body: Native Spanish speaker, fluent in English, learning Portuguese.

memories.title: Saturdays offline
memories.body: I try to stay offline on Saturdays: no work email or Slack until Sunday evening.

memories.title: Japan trip
memories.body: Planning two weeks in Japan in April 2027: Tokyo, Kanazawa and Kyoto, travelling by rail.

memories.title: No car
memories.body: I don't own a car; I get around by metro, bike and the occasional car share.

memories.title: Alcohol
memories.body: I rarely drink, at most a glass of wine at the weekend. I prefer alcohol-free options at events.

memories.title: Swift style
memories.body: Swift: prefer value types and protocols, avoid force unwraps outside tests, use guard for early exits, and keep functions under about 40 lines.

memories.title: Swift concurrency
memories.body: Use async/await and actors instead of completion handlers or GCD in new code, with strict concurrency checking on.

memories.title: Swift Testing
memories.body: New Swift tests use Swift Testing (@Test, #expect), not XCTest, except for UI tests.

memories.title: Python conventions
memories.body: Python scripts: Python 3.12, type hints everywhere, ruff for lint and format, pathlib instead of os.path, and a main() guarded by __name__.

memories.title: TypeScript conventions
memories.body: TypeScript in strict mode, no 'any', zod for runtime validation, pnpm as the package manager.

memories.title: Commit messages
memories.body: Commit messages: imperative subject under 60 characters, a blank line, then why the change was made. No conventional-commit prefixes.

memories.title: Git workflow
memories.body: Feature branches off main, squash-merged via pull request. Rebase rather than merge to update a branch. Never force-push to main.

memories.title: Testing approach
memories.body: Write tests for behaviour, not implementation. Prefer fakes over mocks. A bug fix starts with a failing test.

memories.title: Code review style
memories.body: In code reviews, separate blocking issues from nits and label nits as "nit:". Suggest code rather than only describing the problem.

memories.title: Editors
memories.body: I use Xcode for Swift and Neovim for everything else, with a light theme during the day.

memories.title: Shell tools
memories.body: zsh with a minimal prompt; ripgrep, fd, jq and fzf daily. Prefer one-liners that work with macOS's BSD tools.

memories.title: Third-party dependencies
memories.body: Be conservative with third-party dependencies: pin exact versions, check the licence and maintenance activity, and prefer the standard library.

memories.title: Databases
memories.body: Default to SQLite for local apps and Postgres for servers. Write SQL by hand; avoid heavy ORMs.

memories.title: Documentation
memories.body: Every repository gets a README covering what it does, how to run it and how to test it. Decisions go in short ADRs.

memories.title: Error handling
memories.body: Use typed errors and never swallow errors silently. Log with context but never log user data or secrets.

memories.title: Server logs
memories.body: Server logs must not include request bodies or personal data; IDs and timings only.

memories.title: Continuous integration
memories.body: GitHub Actions for CI: every pull request must pass lint, tests and a build, and pipelines should stay under 10 minutes.

memories.title: Hosting side projects
memories.body: I host side projects on a single Hetzner VPS with Docker Compose and Caddy. No Kubernetes.

memories.title: API design
memories.body: REST APIs: plural nouns, cursor pagination, ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, and error bodies with a machine-readable code.

memories.title: Naming
memories.body: Prefer descriptive names over abbreviations; booleans read as assertions (isEnabled, hasAccess).

memories.title: Code formatting
memories.body: Swift is formatted with swift-format: 4-space indentation and a 120-column limit.

memories.title: Accessibility
memories.body: UI work must support VoiceOver, Dynamic Type and dark mode from the start, not as a follow-up.

memories.title: Performance work
memories.body: Measure before optimizing, and include before/after numbers in pull requests that claim speedups.

memories.title: Secrets in code
memories.body: Never put API keys in source or config files committed to git. Use the Keychain locally and environment variables in CI.

memories.title: Code you write for me
memories.body: When you write code for me, give the complete file or a precise diff, and say what you didn't test.

memories.title: Programming languages I know
memories.body: Strong in Swift, Python, TypeScript and SQL; comfortable with Go; rusty in Java; never used Rust in production.

memories.title: Target platforms
memories.body: My apps target macOS 15+ and iOS 18+. I don't support older OS versions in new projects.

memories.title: Development machine
memories.body: My main machine is a MacBook Pro M1 with 16 GB of RAM; builds shouldn't assume more memory than that.

memories.title: Data analysis
memories.body: For quick data analysis I use Python with pandas in Jupyter, and plain matplotlib charts.

memories.title: Open-source licence
memories.body: My open-source projects use the Apache-2.0 licence.

memories.title: Dates in code
memories.body: Store timestamps in UTC and convert to local time only at the edges. Never parse dates with hand-written regexes.

memories.title: Work in small steps
memories.body: I like to work in small reviewable steps: propose a plan first for anything bigger than one file.

memories.title: Destructive commands
memories.body: Before running destructive shell commands (rm -rf, force-push, dropping tables), stop and ask me.

memories.title: SwiftUI
memories.body: SwiftUI with the Observation framework (@Observable), no Combine in new code, and a preview for every view.

memories.title: Backups of my work
memories.body: Projects live in ~/Projects and are backed up with Time Machine plus a nightly restic job to remote storage.

memories.title: Technical learning goals
memories.body: This year I want to learn Rust well enough to ship a small CLI, and get better at database internals.

memories.title: Harbor app
memories.body: Harbor is a booking app I'm building for the Tejo Sailing Club: members reserve dinghies and instructors. iOS app plus a small Go API.

memories.title: Harbor client contact
memories.body: The Harbor project is paid for by the sailing club. The treasurer, Marta Silva, approves invoices and prefers email to phone calls.

memories.title: Harbor tech stack
memories.body: Harbor: SwiftUI app, Go API on the VPS, Postgres, push notifications via APNs. Payments are out of scope for v1.

memories.title: Harbor milestones
memories.body: Harbor beta to club members by 15 Jan 2027; App Store submission by 1 March 2027.

memories.title: Harbor design decisions
memories.body: Harbor shows bookings in a calendar grid, has a 48-hour cancellation rule, and lets instructors block out times.

memories.title: Harbor's users
memories.body: About 120 club members, many over 60 and not comfortable with technology; large text and simple flows matter.

memories.title: Harbor known issue
memories.body: Harbor beta blocker: booking confirmations show the wrong time zone for members abroad.

memories.title: Ledgerly
memories.body: Ledgerly is my open-source command-line budgeting tool in Python. It imports bank CSV exports and categorizes transactions with rules.

memories.title: Ledgerly roadmap
memories.body: Next for Ledgerly: support for Portuguese bank CSV formats and a monthly report command.

memories.title: Ledgerly community
memories.body: Ledgerly has about 300 GitHub stars and a few regular contributors; I want to keep it dependency-light.

memories.title: Nordwind confidentiality
memories.body: Nordwind's code and data are under NDA. Never paste their code, schemas or customer names into external tools or chatbots.

memories.title: Nordwind contacts
memories.body: At Nordwind my lead is Erik Halvorsen, the CTO. Standups are at 9:30 CET on Tuesdays and Thursdays.

memories.body: Ideas I keep coming back to: a plant-watering reminder app, a recipe scaler, and a CLI that checks weather windows for dinghy sailing.

memories.body: I maintain a small Swift library for parsing GPX files and triage its issues on Sunday evenings.

memories.body: When I travel I keep client work to mornings and stay reachable by email only.

memories.body: For Harbor's Android version I may subcontract to Priya, a Kotlin developer I've worked with before.

memories.title: Task tracking
memories.body: I track client tasks in Linear and personal projects in plain Markdown files.

memories.title: Home address
memories.body: Never share my home address or put it in documents for clients; use the coworking address for business mail.

memories.title: Nieces and nephews
memories.body: Don't mention my sister's children by name or share their photos in anything public.

memories.title: Health information and work
memories.body: Health details must never be shared with work-related agents or included in client communications.

memories.title: Location and routine
memories.body: Don't reveal my real-time location or daily routine (gym times, café visits) to third parties.

memories.title: Screenshots
memories.body: Blur names and email addresses in any screenshot used in blog posts or bug reports.

memories.title: Phone number
memories.body: My phone number is only for family and close friends. Clients get email and Slack.

memories.title: Social media
memories.body: I'm not on Facebook or Instagram, only Mastodon and LinkedIn. Don't suggest posting personal news publicly.

memories.title: Opting out of AI training
memories.body: I prefer tools that don't train on my data, and opt out of model training wherever there's a setting.

memories.title: Analytics in my apps
memories.body: My apps use privacy-preserving analytics only: no third-party trackers and no advertising identifiers.

memories.title: Financial details
memories.body: Don't share my income, account balances or rates with anyone except my accountant.

memories.title: Jordan's privacy
memories.body: Jordan prefers not to be named online; refer to "my partner" in public writing.

memories.title: Photo metadata
memories.body: Strip location metadata from photos before sharing them.

memories.title: Passwords
memories.body: All passwords live in a password manager. Never ask me to paste a password or recovery code into a chat.

memories.title: Email aliases
memories.body: I use a separate email alias for every online service, so sign-ups should use a fresh alias.

memories.title: Recording calls
memories.body: Don't record or transcribe calls without asking everyone on the call first.

memories.title: Client data retention
memories.body: Delete client datasets from my machine within 30 days of a project ending.

memories.title: Penicillin allergy
memories.body: I'm allergic to penicillin (it gives me hives), and to amoxicillin too.

memories.title: Peanut allergy
memories.body: Mild peanut allergy: no peanuts or peanut oil. Tree nuts are fine.

memories.title: Migraines
memories.body: I get migraines about twice a month, often triggered by poor sleep or skipped meals. I take sumatriptan when one starts.

memories.title: Lower back pain
memories.body: My lower back flares up when I sit too long, so I stand every hour and do physio exercises.

memories.title: Physio routine
memories.body: Daily physio routine: cat-cow, bird-dog and glute bridges, about ten minutes.

memories.title: Sleep
memories.body: I aim for 7.5 hours of sleep and to be in bed by 23:00, with screens off 30 minutes before.

memories.title: Caffeine cutoff
memories.body: No caffeine after 14:00 because it ruins my sleep. Decaf or herbal tea in the afternoon.

memories.title: Supplements and medication
memories.body: Vitamin D daily in winter. No regular prescription medication apart from migraine tablets when needed.

memories.title: Family doctor
memories.body: My GP is Dr. Ana Ferreira at the local health centre; I book appointments through the health service app.

memories.title: Dental check-ups
memories.body: Dental check-up every six months; the next one is in December 2026.

memories.title: Eye strain
memories.body: I get eye strain after long screen sessions. I follow the 20-20-20 rule and have computer glasses.

memories.title: Runner's knee
memories.body: Recovering from runner's knee in my left knee: avoid downhill running and keep long runs under 18 km until January.

memories.title: Lactose intolerance
memories.body: I'm slightly lactose intolerant: small amounts of cheese are fine, but I avoid drinking milk.

memories.title: Blood test results
memories.body: Annual blood test in September 2026: everything normal except slightly low iron. The doctor suggested more legumes and leafy greens.

memories.title: Stress and tension headaches
memories.body: When my workload gets heavy I get tension headaches; a 20-minute walk helps more than anything.

memories.title: Therapy sessions
memories.body: I see a therapist every other Thursday evening; don't schedule anything then.

memories.title: Vaccinations
memories.body: Flu shot every October; tetanus booster due in 2029.

memories.title: Drinking water
memories.body: Remind me to drink water during long coding sessions; I forget.

memories.title: Heart-rate zones
memories.body: Easy runs at a heart rate under 145 bpm; my measured maximum is 188.

memories.title: Protein intake
memories.body: As a vegetarian runner I aim for about 100 g of protein a day from eggs, tofu, tempeh and lentils.

memories.title: Health insurance
memories.body: Private health insurance through my employer-independent plan; it partly covers dental.

memories.title: Sun protection
memories.body: Fair skin that burns easily: SPF 50 for sailing and running, plus a hat.

memories.title: Hay fever
memories.body: Seasonal pollen allergy in April and May; cetirizine helps.

memories.title: Running shoes
memories.body: I run in neutral cushioned shoes and replace them every 700 km.

memories.title: Bank accounts

memories.title: Monthly budget
memories.body: Monthly budget: rent €1,350, groceries €450, transport €60, eating out €200. I review it on the first Sunday of the month.

memories.title: Emergency fund
memories.body: Keep six months of expenses as an emergency fund; currently at about four months.

memories.title: Investing approach
memories.body: Low-cost index funds only, with monthly automatic contributions. No individual stocks.

memories.title: Retirement plan
memories.body: Contribute to a Portuguese PPR retirement plan every December for the tax deduction.

memories.title: Freelance social security
memories.body: As a self-employed freelancer I file quarterly social security declarations in January, April, July and October.

memories.title: Annual tax return
memories.body: The annual income tax return is due between April and June; my accountant files it.

memories.title: Accountant
memories.body: My accountant, Rui Costa, handles taxes and VAT. Send him invoices and receipts by the 10th of each month.

memories.title: VAT on invoices
memories.body: I charge 23% VAT to Portuguese clients; EU business clients get the reverse charge, with their VAT number on the invoice.

memories.title: Quarterly VAT returns
memories.body: VAT returns are quarterly, due by the 20th of the second month after each quarter ends.

memories.title: Invoicing terms
memories.body: Invoices are due net 30 and are issued on the last working day of the month through certified invoicing software.

memories.title: Late payments
memories.body: If a client is more than 15 days late, send a polite payment reminder; after 30 days, a firmer one that mentions late fees.

memories.title: Currency for quotes
memories.body: Quote prices in euros; UK clients may pay in pounds at the day's exchange rate.

memories.title: Subscriptions
memories.body: Review subscriptions every quarter and cancel anything I haven't used in two months.

memories.title: Rent payment
memories.body: Rent is €1,350, paid on the 1st by bank transfer to the landlord, Mr. Duarte.

memories.title: Business expenses
memories.body: Keep receipts for hardware, software, coworking and conference travel; they're business expenses.

memories.title: Buying a flat
memories.body: Considering buying a flat in 2028; I'd need about €60,000 for the down payment and costs.

memories.title: Insurance renewals
memories.body: Home contents insurance and professional liability insurance both renew in February.

memories.title: Donations
memories.body: I donate 2% of my income each year, split between a climate charity and a local food bank.

memories.title: Supporting my parents
memories.body: I send my parents €200 a month by transfer; the amount can vary with the exchange rate.

memories.title: No crypto
memories.body: I don't buy cryptocurrency or NFTs and don't want suggestions about them.

memories.title: Which card to use
memories.body: Use the credit card for travel bookings because of its travel insurance; the debit card for everything else.

memories.title: Spending tracking
memories.body: I track spending with Ledgerly in these categories: housing, food, transport, health, fun and business.

memories.title: Income

memories.title: Japan trip budget
memories.body: Budget for the April 2027 Japan trip: €4,000 for two people, not counting flights.

memories.title: Paying for the renovation
memories.body: The kitchen renovation will be paid from savings, not with a loan.

memories.title: Rental lease
memories.body: The rental lease runs until 31 August 2027. Notice of non-renewal must be given 120 days before, and rent increases are capped by law.

memories.title: Business structure
memories.body: I work as a self-employed sole trader, not a company. I'm considering forming a limited company in 2027 if income keeps growing.

memories.title: Client contracts
memories.body: Every client engagement needs a signed contract with scope, payment terms, IP assignment on full payment, and liability capped at the fees paid.

memories.title: NDAs
memories.body: I sign mutual NDAs only; one-way NDAs need review by my lawyer first.

memories.title: Lawyer
memories.body: My lawyer, Inês Matos, reviews contracts over €10,000 and anything with non-compete clauses.

memories.title: Non-compete clauses
memories.body: Never accept a non-compete clause longer than six months.

memories.title: Will
memories.body: I have a will, drafted in 2025, naming Jordan as executor; the original is with the notary.

memories.title: Residency status
memories.body: I'm an EU citizen living in Portugal with a registration certificate.

memories.title: GDPR for Harbor
memories.body: Harbor stores members' names, phone numbers and booking history. The sailing club is the data controller and I'm the processor under a data processing agreement.

memories.title: App privacy labels
memories.body: Every app I ship needs an accurate App Store privacy label and a privacy policy page.

memories.title: Ledgerly name
memories.body: I checked that the name Ledgerly has no trademark conflict in the EU; it isn't registered.

memories.title: Contributor terms
memories.body: Ledgerly accepts contributions under the DCO sign-off; no CLA.

memories.title: IP ownership
memories.body: Code I write for clients belongs to them once paid; I keep the right to reuse general-purpose utilities.

memories.title: Power of attorney
memories.body: My sister Lucía holds power of attorney for my affairs in Uruguay.

memories.title: Dispute with a former client
memories.body: A small claim against a former client over an unpaid €2,400 invoice settled in July 2026. Don't work with them again.

memories.title: Reading terms of service
memories.body: When summarizing terms of service, flag data sharing, auto-renewal, arbitration and liability limits.
